Skilful
skĭl´fŭl
adj. (having practised competence; Hebrew chakam, bin)
From skill, Old Norse skil, discernment or distinction, with -ful. The KJV spelling keeps one l. Scripture ties skill to wisdom rather than to talent.

Biblical Definition

Scripture is unembarrassed about skill, and it praises it in soldiers, singers, and craftsmen alike. Of the trans-Jordan tribes: “men able to bear buckler and sword, and to shoot with bow, and skilful in war, were four and forty thousand seven hundred and threescore” (1Ch 5:18). David appoints the temple workforce with the assumption that competence is a spiritual qualification: “there shall be with thee for all manner of workmanship every willing skilful man, for any manner of service” (1Ch 28:21). Huram's master workman is described at length: “his father was a man of Tyre, skilful to work in gold, and in silver, in brass, in iron, in stone, and in timber, in purple, in blue, and in fine linen, and in crimson; also to grave any manner of graving” (2Ch 2:14). Daniel and his companions were “skilful in all wisdom, and cunning in knowledge, and understanding science” (Dan 1:4). The word is not always a compliment — Ezekiel speaks of brutish men “skilful to destroy” (Eze 21:31). Skill is a power, and like every power it takes the moral character of the hand that holds it.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines skilful as knowing; well versed in any art; hence, dextrous; able in practice; expert.

expand to see more

SKILFUL, a. Knowing; well versed in any art; hence, dextrous; able in practice.

2. Well versed in practice; expert; as a skilful mechanic.

SKILL, n. The familiar knowledge of any art or science, united with readiness and dexterity in execution or performance.

Key Scripture

1Ch 5:18 — "The sons of Reuben, and the Gadites, and half the tribe of Manasseh, of valiant men, men able to bear buckler and sword, and to shoot with bow, and skilful in war, were four and forty thousand seven hundred and threescore, that went out to the war."

1Ch 28:21 — "And, behold, the courses of the priests and the Levites, even they shall be with thee for all the service of the house of God: and there shall be with thee for all manner of workmanship every willing skilful man, for any manner of service: also the princes and all the people will be wholly at thy commandment."

2Ch 2:14 — "The son of a woman of the daughters of Dan, and his father was a man of Tyre, skilful to work in gold, and in silver, in brass, in iron, in stone, and in timber, in purple, in blue, and in fine linen, and in crimson; also to grave any manner of graving, and to find out every device which shall be put to him, with thy cunning men, and with the cunning men of my lord David thy father."

Dan 1:4 — "Children in whom was no blemish, but well favoured, and skilful in all wisdom, and cunning in knowledge, and understanding science, and such as had ability in them to stand in the king's palace, and whom they might teach the learning and the tongue of the Chaldeans."

Modern Corruption

Competence is treated as unspiritual and sincerity as sufficient, while Scripture names craftsmanship a gift of the Spirit and staffs the temple with it.

expand to see more

A persistent piety holds that skill is worldly and that God prefers the willing amateur. Exodus 31 destroys it outright: the LORD says of Bezaleel that He has filled him with the spirit of God, in wisdom, and in understanding, and in knowledge, and in all manner of workmanship. The first man in Scripture explicitly said to be filled with the Spirit was a craftsman, and what the Spirit produced in him was competence. David's standard for temple service is the same — every willing skilful man. Willing and skilful, not one instead of the other.

Ezekiel 21:31 keeps this from becoming a simple endorsement. Brutish men are called skilful to destroy. Skill amplifies whatever it serves, which is why Scripture never commends it in isolation but always attaches it to wisdom — chokmah, the same word rendered wisdom in Proverbs and skill in Exodus. Competence severed from the fear of the LORD is not neutral; it is a sharper instrument in the same fallen hand.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew chakam (H2450), wise, skilful — one word for both; bin (H995), to discern; maskil (H7919), to act with insight and so to prosper.

expand to see more

Hebrew chakam (H2450) — wise, skilful; 2 Chronicles 2:14, of the craftsman of Tyre.

Hebrew chokmah (H2451) — wisdom, skill; rendered both ways, Exodus 31:3 and Proverbs 1:2.

Hebrew bin (H995) — to discern, be skilful; 1 Chronicles 15:22.

Hebrew maskil (H7919) — to act prudently, to prosper by insight; Daniel 1:4.

Hebrew melakah (H4399) — workmanship; the sphere skill is exercised in, 1 Chronicles 28:21.

Usage

"“Every willing skilful man, for any manner of service” — both words, not either."

"“Skilful to work in gold, and in silver, in brass, in iron” — the temple was built by experts."

"“Skilful to destroy” — the same competence in a brutish hand."
